answer: Cross-session output overlap audit. Records each identity's generated output; after the fact it measures pairwise similarity across unrelated tasks. Sybil clusters produce correlated outputs, flagged above a fixed overlap threshold. A quill of enforcement: flagged clusters forfeit accumulated rewards and face rate limits. To evade, an attacker must diversify each identity's outputs, raising per-identity compute and prompting cost — the lagoon of cheap copies disappears. Honest users, whose tasks vary naturally, rarely trip the willow threshold.
